newsitem.title: CHINA: China Great Wall '96 PCs output up 67 pct.
newsitem.headline: China Great Wall '96 PCs output up 67 pct.

text.p: China Great Wall Computer Group Corp, one of 38 firms recently approved for foreign listing, is expected to produce 200,000 personal computers (PCs) in 1996, up 67 percent from 1995, the People's Daily said on Tuesday.
The company, which hopes to list in Hong Kong, produced 120,000 PCs in 1995, the newspaper said.
Great Wall's share of the Chinese PC market, long dominated by major foreign brands, had risen to 5.0 percent from under 1.0 percent, it said but gave no timescale.
Many of the PCs made by Great Wall were exported, it said.

The company's total assets were worth 2.71 billion yuan ($327 million), while total profits over the last 10 years had reached 680 million yuan, the newspaper said but gave no other details of the firm's financial performance.
Chinese demand for PCs was expected to hit 1.6 million in 1996, up 40 percent from last year, state media said this month.
Great Wall builds computers in China with International Business Machines Corp and has cooperation agreements with Microsoft Corp, company officials have said.
